Increasing acquisition cost (mature markets, less effective ads) · demand for relationship-based marketing · declining brand loyalty and higher switching.
A deeply held commitment to re-buy or re-patronise a preferred product in the future despite situational influences and marketing efforts that could cause switching (HBR, 2010).

Satisfaction is positively associated with customer-level outcomes (retention, WOM, spending, price) and firm-level outcomes (product-market, accounting, financial-market performance); varies by context (Mittal et al., 2023).
The present value of the future (net) cash flows associated with a (typical) customer. Forward-looking, predictive not precise, use only relevant data.
Traditional: market share, sales growth. Acquisition: acquisition rate, acquisition cost. Activity: average inter-purchase time, retention/attrition, survival rate, lifetime duration.

Acquisition rate = 100 × prospects acquired / prospects targeted.
Acquisition cost = acquisition spending / prospects acquired.
Rr_t = customers buying in t (who bought in t−1) / customers who bought in t−1. Rr = 100% − defection rate. Average lifetime = 1 / (1 − Rr).
Average lifetime = Σ (t × number of retained customers in t) / N (cohort size).
CLV = lifetime revenues (or margin) − acquisition costs. E.g. 10 € × 12 × 10 years − 200 € = 1,000 €.
CLV = annual revenue × lifetime × (1 − overhead %) − CAC. Education: 3,000 × 5 × 0.8 − 1,500 = 10,500.
Monthly margin = margin/transaction × frequency. Rr = (start − lost)/start. SR = Rr × previous SR. Profit = margin × SR (− CAC in month 1). Compare cumulative profits.
